title: Double Column Transposition Reloaded, parts 1-3
origin: Challenge by Arno Wacker, Bernhard Esslinger and Klaus Schmeh, published on MysteryTwister in December 2013

part1.published_facts: English plaintext. Both keys have 20-27 letters, with co-prime lengths, and were derived from English sentences.

part2.published_facts: Two English texts interleaved word by word. Both keys have 20-27 letters, with co-prime lengths, and were chosen at random.

part3.published_facts: German plaintext. Both keys have 27-34 letters, with co-prime lengths, and were chosen at random.

full_solution: The two keys and the complete plaintext of all three parts.

verification.how: For each part the two submitted keys are applied to the ciphertext and must produce the submitted plaintext exactly. The answer counts once MysteryTwister's solution check accepts the first 34, 37 and 48 letters of the three plaintexts.

notes: MysteryTwister listed 0 solves for each part on 2026-11-15.

sources.what: Challenge list with ciphertext files and descriptions

published_facts.fact: The three challenges were built with the weaknesses in mind that had been used to solve the first challenge of this kind, set in 2007 and solved in 2013.
Part 3: the plaintext was written by the authors themselves and not taken from any published source.
The first challenge was solved by George Lasry with a hill-climbing attack on the ciphertext alone and a dictionary attack on keys made from phrases.
published_facts.source: Lasry, Kopal and Wacker, Solving the Double Transposition Challenge with a Divide-and-Conquer Approach, Cryptologia 38(3), 2014
published_facts.checked: Abstract and the post by Klaus Schmeh; the paper itself was not read.

published_facts.fact: George Lasry reported in 2018 that his hill-climbing method could not produce a solution for these challenges, and that for part 1 he had tested tens of billions of phrases from Wikipedia and Project Gutenberg as the second key.
